Definition: from the same as G3693 with enclitic of direction; to the back, i.e. aback (as adverb or preposition of time or place; or as noun):--after, back(-ward), (+ get) behind, + follow.
BiblicalUsage: After can mean place or time. John the Baptist said, He that cometh after me is preferred before me, for He was before me, and Gamaliel reminded the council how Judas of Galilee drew away much people after him.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that what comes after matters: John knew the One coming after him was before him, and I follow the same order.
